generator: commit a wav per lesson; this file is the script, not audio

voice_spec.role: Professional YouTube-tutorial narrator, the same voice as the existing On-Chain Operator renders
voice_spec.delivery: Calm, clear, adult, second person. One idea per sentence. Not a character and not a hype read.
voice_spec.music: Do not mix music into the wav. course/render/render_tutorial.py ducks the licensed bed under this track.
voice_spec.alignment: Speak beats in order. Each beat's target length is beats[].seconds. The file should land within a few seconds of target_seconds so the outro is not clipped by -shortest.

beats.vo: Price often chops sideways, weaving through the same band instead of leaving. A grid is a ladder of limit orders built for that weave, and it has nothing to do while price runs one way and stays there. On the diagram for this beat, look for a sideways path inside a band, then the same path stepping out the bottom and not returning. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Sketch a band and a weave on a blank page, and write the word Example at the top. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. This picture is not a claim that the next day will chop. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hook. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Education only, not financial advice. Crypto and DeFi carry significant risk, including total loss of capital. This is general information. It does not consider your objectives, financial situation, or needs. Past or example results do not indicate future results. Consider independent advice. We do not sell or run a trading bot.
This is the Grid Bot Blueprint. The lesson is Introduction. Navy and cyan on the frame. Education only. You will write on paper before any screen.

A grid has three parts you can name: the range, the levels, and the stop. The range is the band. The levels are the rungs inside it. The stop is the written line where the idea is finished. On the diagram for this beat, look for three callouts on one band: Range on the outer lines, Levels on the rungs, Stop under the band. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the three words as headings, with one blank line under each. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. If you can only name one of them, the page is not ready. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The three parts. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The range is a top and a bottom you draw before any rung. Without a top and a bottom, a spacing percent is a number floating in the margin. On the diagram for this beat, look for two horizontal lines first, rungs added only after both lines exist. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw the upper line and the lower line, and leave the middle empty for one breath. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Do not start from a grid count and hope a range appears. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The range. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The levels are limit orders that wait on the rungs. A limit order sits at a price. It does not chase. A market order that cuts through the book is a different tool. On the diagram for this beat, look for markers waiting on rungs, and a faded arrow wrongly cutting through them. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Put a small dot on four rungs and write Waits beside the dots. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Waiting is the mechanism. It is not a promise that a fill will happen. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The levels. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

One approach places buy orders below the mark and sell orders above it. As price weaves down, buys are the orders that can fill. As it weaves up, sells are. If price leaves, one side is left holding inventory. On the diagram for this beat, look for buy dots below a centre line and sell dots above it, inside one band. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Mark a centre line, then four buys below and four sells above, and label the page Example. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. This is one teaching picture, not the only way a person might arrange orders. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Buys and sells. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The stop is a sentence you write, not a feeling that the trade is over. The sentence names the price path that finishes the idea, usually a path that leaves the band and does not come back. On the diagram for this beat, look for a dashed line under the band and a path that exits and stays out. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write one stop sentence in plain words under the sketch. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A blank stop means the page has no end, so every later click inherits that hole. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The stop. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

We do not sell or run a trading bot. No order is sent from this lesson. You draw the idea. If a screen appears later, it should be a copy of the page, and only on paper or demo. On the diagram for this beat, look for a notebook page with an arrow toward a blank generic form, the form empty until the page is filled. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write this line at the top of the notebook: no order is sent from the lesson. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A course video cannot place, cancel, or watch an order for you. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to We do not run it. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The course is a map, and this introduction is only the first square. Next is a checklist, then the definition, then regimes, then spacing and range, then entry and exit, then a paper screen, then monitoring, then mistakes, then scaling, then an opt-in lesson on liquidation. On the diagram for this beat, look for a ten-step path with only the first step lit. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Copy the next three titles into the notebook so the map is on paper. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. If someone told you the introduction was the whole class, they skipped the map. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The map. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Draw a path that leaves the top of the band and does not return. The rungs below are still there, but the weave they were built for is gone. Inventory can sit on one side. On the diagram for this beat, look for a path exiting the top and a stack of unfilled rungs left behind. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Add that exiting path to the sketch and circle the rungs that no longer get crossed. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A grid that looked tidy inside the band is not automatically tidy outside it. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to When the drawing fails. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

There is no result number in this lesson. A result number would pretend the example already happened. The example is a drawing of a mechanism. On the diagram for this beat, look for an empty results box crossed out beside the band diagram. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. If you wrote a profit figure, cross it out and write Example instead. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Past or imagined results do not indicate future results. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to No result number. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A slow sketch uses eight even ticks inside the band, only as a way to see rungs. Eight is not a setting this lesson tells you to use. It is a count you can point at while you learn the word level. On the diagram for this beat, look for eight even ticks inside a band, captioned Example, not a recommended count. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw eight ticks, then write beside them: this count is for practice. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Copying eight onto a live screen would be changing the subject. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Eight ticks. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The next step is the setup checklist, on paper, before any screen. You will need the three words when that checklist asks what a grid is. On the diagram for this beat, look for an arrow from the three headings to a checklist page. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write one line: my next step is the setup checklist. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Do not open a live order ticket as the next step. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The checklist is next. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A paper or demo account is a fence around practice. Inside the fence you can see fields and buttons. You still do not send an order in this course. On the diagram for this beat, look for a dashed fence around a worksheet, with the live side left blank. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write Paper at the top of the page you will use for the rest of the course. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Feeling ready is not the same thing as having the page. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Paper first. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Your turn, still inside The three parts. Cover the notes and say this from memory: A grid has three parts you can name: the range, the levels, and the stop. Then uncover the diagram and check that you can still see three callouts on one band: Range on the outer lines, Levels on the rungs, Stop under the band. Write the three words as headings, with one blank line under each. Write one check question a classmate could answer from the drawing alone, and write the answer under it. The answer has to name a shape on the page. An answer about what the market will do is the wrong kind of answer. This is practice on paper. No order is sent.

If you keep one sentence, keep this: range, levels, and stop, drawn before any click. The weave is the job. The exit from the band is the failure picture. No result number belongs on the page. On the diagram for this beat, look for three recap rows with a tiny band, a tiny ladder, and a tiny stop. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Read the three rows out loud and point at each sketch. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The introduction is the map, not the last lesson. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to One sentence to keep. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.
Next lesson: What you are going to need. Bring the page you just wrote. Leave every example marked Example. No order is sent between lessons.

beats.vo: You need a page before you need a screen. People lose the lesson when they open a form while the notebook is still blank. On the diagram for this beat, look for a blank checklist beside a dimmed generic form. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Open a fresh page and write the lesson title at the top. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A screen cannot supply a fact you have not written. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hook. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The setup check has seven lines: notebook, the three words, pair name, paper or demo, no secrets, a written stop, and the word Example. Each line is a fact. A tick without the fact is decoration. On the diagram for this beat, look for a seven-row checklist with simple icons and one row highlighted. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the seven labels down the page, leaving a blank answer line on each. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Seven ticks on an empty page is not a finished check. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Seven items. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The three words are range, levels, and stop, carried forward from the introduction. The checklist asks for them so a later form has something true to copy. On the diagram for this beat, look for three labelled chips feeding one checklist row. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write a one-line definition under each word, in your own words. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. If the definition does not match the diagram, the diagram wins and you rewrite the line. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The three words. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A pair name is two assets written with a slash, such as the base and the quote. An empty pair slot is a missing fact. It is not a detail you will remember later. On the diagram for this beat, look for two empty tags joined by a slash, one tag circled. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write a practice pair and the word Example, so it cannot be read as a pick. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. This lesson does not choose a market for you. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Pair name. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The screen, when you reach it, is paper or demo. Paper lets you see the fields. It does not send an order, and this course never asks you to send one. On the diagram for this beat, look for a fence around a generic form labelled Paper. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write Paper or demo on the checklist, and leave the live box empty. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A live ticket is not the assignment. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Paper or demo. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

You never type a seed phrase, a private key, or an API secret into a lesson, a chat, or a form. The course can teach the shape of a field. It cannot be trusted with a secret, and it will not ask. On the diagram for this beat, look for a key shape crossed out next to an empty form. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write this rule on the checklist in your own handwriting. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Anyone who asks for the phrase is outside this course. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to No secrets. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The stop line on the checklist is a sentence, not a tick. The sentence says what path finishes the idea. A tick with no sentence is the common miss. On the diagram for this beat, look for a checklist row with a sentence line, and a faded tick that has no sentence. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draft one stop sentence even if you revise it in a later lesson. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. You are not being told a price to use. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Written stop. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Every number and every pair on the page carries the word Example. That word is what keeps a teaching sketch from being read as a recommendation. On the diagram for this beat, look for a stamp that says Example on the corner of the page. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Add the stamp before you add any figure. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A page without that word is not ready to be copied onto a form. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The word Example. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A profit target is not on the list. A leverage multiple is not on the list. Those lines would change the subject from setup to a result, and this lesson has no result. On the diagram for this beat, look for two crossed-out rows under the real seven. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Speed here deletes the only record you have. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Common miss. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The action is to complete the seven lines on paper today. Read each answer out loud. If a line has no answer, it is not done. On the diagram for this beat, look for a completed seven-row page with a pencil on the last row. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Sign the bottom with the date you will reread it, not a date you promise to trade. A grid bot is not a machine that predicts price. It is a set of waiting limit orders inside a band you chose. If the sentence gives the thinking to the bot, the sentence is from a different course. On the diagram for this beat, look for a ladder of waiting orders with a question mark on a crystal-ball shape that is crossed out. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the definition in one line before you watch the rest. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Automation can place the orders you already wrote. It does not decide the band. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hook. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

This is the Grid Bot Blueprint. The lesson is What is a grid bot. Navy and cyan on the frame. Education only. You will write on paper before any screen.

Five labels cover the picture: upper, lower, levels, side, and stop. Upper and lower are the band. Levels are the rungs. Side is which inventory you hold when price moves. Stop is the written end. On the diagram for this beat, look for a band with five callout tags, each tag touching the part it names. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the five labels and draw a line from each word to the part. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A label that does not touch a part is decoration. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Five labels. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Limit orders wait at a price. They do not jump the queue. A market order pays through the book now. That is a different tool, and it is not what these rungs are. On the diagram for this beat, look for a waiting marker on a level beside a faded market arrow cutting through. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write Waits under one rung and Not this tool under the arrow. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Waiting can mean no fill. That outcome belongs in the picture. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Limit orders wait. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

When price steps down through a rung, a buy limit that was waiting there can fill. You then hold a little more of the base asset, and a sell can be written one rung higher. That is the weave, told as inventory, not as a result. On the diagram for this beat, look for a price tick crossing one buy rung, with a small inventory box growing by one unit marked Example. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Number two rungs and narrate one step-down with your finger. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. One fill in a drawing is not a forecast of fills. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Price steps down. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

When price steps up through a rung, a sell limit that was waiting there can fill. Inventory of the base can fall, and the quote asset can rise, inside the example. On the diagram for this beat, look for a price tick crossing one sell rung, inventory box shrinking, labelled Example. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Narrate one step-up on the same sketch. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The two steps together are the mechanism. Neither step is a target. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Price steps up. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Inventory is what you hold when the fills are uneven. If price leaves the band, the fills stop being a weave and become a pile on one side. On the diagram for this beat, look for a balanced pair of boxes inside the band, and a single heavy box after an exit. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw both pictures and write Inside and Outside under them. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The heavy box is not a profit figure. It is a mix of assets. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Inventory. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The bot's job, if you use one, is to keep the written rungs in the market. The job is clerical. The band, the count, and the stop stay yours. On the diagram for this beat, look for a short list of rungs with a clerical check mark, and a separate human-drawn band. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write two columns: Mine and Clerical. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. We do not sell or run the bot that would do the clerical part. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The bot's job. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Say the five labels while you point: upper, lower, levels, side, stop. Your ear can nod and still miss a word. The point of saying them is to find the miss. On the diagram for this beat, look for five tags in a row, the third one highlighted as the one people skip. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Cover the page and say the five from memory, then check. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Four out of five is not the pass. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Say the five. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The path on the diagram is hypothetical noise, drawn so you can see crossings. It is not a chart of a day that happened, and it is not a path you should expect. On the diagram for this beat, look for a dashed weave labelled Example through even rungs. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Add the word Hypothetical on the path. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. If the path looks like a promise, redraw it as a dashed example. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hypothetical path. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A common miss is to describe the bot as earning while price chops. The mechanism is fills and inventory. A result would require a future that this page does not have. On the diagram for this beat, look for a results box crossed out next to a clean ladder. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Cross out any earnings word you wrote. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Education describes the machine. It does not forecast the machine. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Common miss. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

No exchange is a partner in this definition. The picture is generic so the definition survives a different screen. On the diagram for this beat, look for a generic ladder with logos absent and a small no-logo mark. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. If you sketched a logo, erase it. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The next lessons still will not send you to a live ticket. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Not affiliated. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

In one breath: waiting limit orders, inside a band, with a written stop, and inventory that changes as rungs fill. That sentence is the whole definition. A line that says the weave cannot fail does not belong in it. On the diagram for this beat, look for one sentence boxed on a card, with the ladder behind it. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the sentence from memory. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The regime lesson is next, because a definition does not tell you when the band is a poor fit. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to One-breath definition. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

On paper, label a band with the five words and tell the step-down once. Do it before the regime lesson so the words are already in your handwriting. On the diagram for this beat, look for a finished five-label sketch and a pencil. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Leave the page in the notebook. Do not copy it to a live form. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The action is the labelling, not an order. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Paper check. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Your turn, still inside Five labels. Cover the notes and say this from memory: Five labels cover the picture: upper, lower, levels, side, and stop. Then uncover the diagram and check that you can still see a band with five callout tags, each tag touching the part it names. Write the five labels and draw a line from each word to the part. Write one check question a classmate could answer from the drawing alone, and write the answer under it. The answer has to name a shape on the page. An answer about what the market will do is the wrong kind of answer. This is practice on paper. No order is sent.

Your turn, still inside Limit orders wait. Cover the notes and say this from memory: Limit orders wait at a price. They do not jump the queue. Then uncover the diagram and check that you can still see a waiting marker on a level beside a faded market arrow cutting through. Write Waits under one rung and Not this tool under the arrow. Write one check question a classmate could answer from the drawing alone, and write the answer under it. The answer has to name a shape on the page. An answer about what the market will do is the wrong kind of answer. This is practice on paper. No order is sent.

It is not a signal, not a fund, and not a person watching the market for you. If a sentence needs one of those, delete the sentence and return to the five labels. On the diagram for this beat, look for three crossed-out icons for a signal flare, a vault, and an eye, beside the ladder. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write Is not under the definition and list those three. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The clerical tool remains optional and outside this video. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to What the bot is not. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.
Next lesson: Market regimes. Bring the page you just wrote. Leave every example marked Example. No order is sent between lessons.

The same ladder is a different idea in a different regime. A weave inside a band is the picture the ladder was built for. A one-way run is the picture that leaves it behind. On the diagram for this beat, look for two small charts with the same ladder: one weaving, one leaving. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Title the page Regimes, and write Example under it. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. No one is telling you what tomorrow's regime will be. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hook. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

This is the Grid Bot Blueprint. The lesson is Market regimes. Navy and cyan on the frame. Education only. You will write on paper before any screen.

Three shapes are enough for this lesson: range, trend, and break. Range weaves. Trend walks one way with pullbacks. Break leaves a level and does not return on the sketch. On the diagram for this beat, look for three panels labelled Range, Trend, and Break. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw the three shapes before you draw any grid on them. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A fourth name is optional. These three have to be obvious first. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Three shapes. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

You sort the path before you choose a spacing. Spacing a band you have not described is how a tight grid meets a break. On the diagram for this beat, look for a sorting arrow that comes before a spacing percent, the percent faded. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the sort as the first line of the page. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The sort is a label for the drawing in front of you, not a forecast. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Sort first. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A range is the shape where a grid's waiting orders can be crossed more than once on the sketch. That is a description of the drawing. It is not a claim that a range will continue. On the diagram for this beat, look for a weave crossing the same three rungs more than once. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Circle one rung that the example path crosses twice. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Twice on a sketch is a teaching device. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Range fit. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A trend on this page is a path that makes higher highs or lower lows, with small pullbacks. A grid in that picture spends more time adding inventory on one side. On the diagram for this beat, look for a staircase path with inventory piling on the lower rungs. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw the pile and write One side under it. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The pile is inventory, not a result. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Trend. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A break leaves the band and does not return on the sketch. Orders left inside the old band are no longer being crossed. The stop sentence is the tool you already wrote for this picture. On the diagram for this beat, look for a path exiting and a stop line already on the page. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Point at the stop sentence and read it against the exiting path. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The lesson does not tell you a price at which to exit. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Break. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Work one example path from left to right and give it one label. Say which of the three shapes it is, and say one reason from the drawing, not from a hope. On the diagram for this beat, look for one path with a single label chip and a one-line reason. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the label and the reason. Add Example. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. If you have two labels, you do not have a sort yet. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Worked sort. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

beats.chapter: What you do with the label
beats.vo: The label decides whether the ladder is even the tool on the page. Range keeps the ladder in the conversation. Trend makes you draw the inventory pile before you go on. Break sends you to the stop sentence. On the diagram for this beat, look for three arrows from the three shapes to Ladder, Pile, and Stop. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Copy those three arrows. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The label is not an order to click anything. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to What you do with the label. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

An ordinary day on this page means the size of weave you already drew, not a promise about tomorrow. If your band is thinner than that drawn weave, the path leaves by construction. On the diagram for this beat, look for a weave wider than a thin band, the path outside. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Compare the height of the weave to the height of the band with a bracket. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. You are comparing drawings. You are not measuring the future. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Ordinary day. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A path into a major news bar, or a thin book, is a poor place to pretend you have a calm range. The sketch can show a gap bar that jumps the rungs instead of weaving them. On the diagram for this beat, look for a gap bar jumping several rungs, rungs left untouched. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw one jump bar and write Jumped, not wove. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. This is a caution about the picture, not a calendar of events. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to News and thin books. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The common miss is to pick the grid first and the regime second. Then every path gets a ladder, including the path that leaves. On the diagram for this beat, look for a ladder stamped on all three shapes, the stamp crossed out on Trend and Break. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Cross out the ladder on the two shapes where you said it does not belong yet. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. You can still study those shapes. You do not have to force the tool. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Common miss. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The sentence to keep: name the shape, then decide whether a ladder belongs on it. Range, trend, and break are the three names. The stop sentence meets the break. On the diagram for this beat, look for three chips and one sentence under them. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Say the sentence without looking, then check. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Spacing comes next, and only after this sort. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to One sentence. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Sort one hypothetical path on paper into range, trend, or break, and write one reason. Use a path you draw yourself so you are not copying a live chart's implication. On the diagram for this beat, look for a handmade path and a label. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. File it behind the checklist. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Do not replace the handmade path with a live ticker as the assignment. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Paper sort. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Your turn, still inside Three shapes. Cover the notes and say this from memory: Three shapes are enough for this lesson: range, trend, and break. Then uncover the diagram and check that you can still see three panels labelled Range, Trend, and Break. Draw the three shapes before you draw any grid on them. Write one check question a classmate could answer from the drawing alone, and write the answer under it. The answer has to name a shape on the page. An answer about what the market will do is the wrong kind of answer. This is practice on paper. No order is sent.

Your turn, still inside Sort first. Cover the notes and say this from memory: You sort the path before you choose a spacing. Then uncover the diagram and check that you can still see a sorting arrow that comes before a spacing percent, the percent faded. Write the sort as the first line of the page. Write one check question a classmate could answer from the drawing alone, and write the answer under it. The answer has to name a shape on the page. An answer about what the market will do is the wrong kind of answer. This is practice on paper. No order is sent.

Your turn, still inside Range fit. Cover the notes and say this from memory: A range is the shape where a grid's waiting orders can be crossed more than once on the sketch. Then uncover the diagram and check that you can still see a weave crossing the same three rungs more than once. Circle one rung that the example path crosses twice. Write one check question a classmate could answer from the drawing alone, and write the answer under it. The answer has to name a shape on the page. An answer about what the market will do is the wrong kind of answer. This is practice on paper. No order is sent.

This lesson does not give you a score that says go. A score would hide the sort inside a number. The sort has to stay visible. On the diagram for this beat, look for a numeric gauge crossed out beside a clear three-shape key. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. If you wrote a score, replace it with the word you can point at. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Visible labels are the whole method here. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to No score. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.
Next lesson: Choosing grid spacing and range. Bring the page you just wrote. Leave every example marked Example. No order is sent between lessons.

A band that is too tight can break on an ordinary weave you already drew. The tight band is not braver. It is smaller than the path, so the path leaves. On the diagram for this beat, look for a thin band and a taller weave that exits it. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw a weave first, then a band that fails to cover it, and mark the exit. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Ordinary here means the drawing, not a forecast. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hook. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

This is the Grid Bot Blueprint. The lesson is Choosing grid spacing and range. Navy and cyan on the frame. Education only. You will write on paper before any screen.

Twenty order lines make nineteen gaps. You multiply the step by the gaps, not by the lines. Counting lines as gaps makes the band one step too tall. On the diagram for this beat, look for twenty lines with nineteen marked gaps between them. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Count the gaps out loud from one to nineteen on a sketch of twenty lines. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The house count is a teaching count, not a setting you must use. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Gaps and orders. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Nineteen gaps times a half of one percent is a span of nine and a half percent from the lower line to the upper line. That arithmetic is the check. If your page says ten percent for twenty lines at a half percent, you counted lines. On the diagram for this beat, look for a band labelled nine and a half percent, with nineteen gaps, stamped Example. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write 19 gaps, 0.5 percent step, 9.5 percent span, and the word Example. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. These figures are a counting example. They are not levels to trade. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to The span. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Halving the step without recounting the gaps doubles the line count for the same span, and the new gap count is not the old line count. If the span stays nine and a half percent and the step becomes a quarter of one percent, the gap count is thirty-eight, not forty. On the diagram for this beat, look for the same span split into finer gaps, with the wrong count forty crossed out. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the wrong count and the right count side by side. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The point is the recount. It is not a finer grid you are told to run. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Half spacing. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A spacing percent without a range is a number in the margin. The range says where the band sits. The spacing says how the band is cut. The range comes first. On the diagram for this beat, look for a range bracket drawn before a row of gap marks. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write Range, then Spacing, as two headings in that order. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Starting from a percent you like is the miss. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Range first. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A gap smaller than the cost of a buy and a sell can be flat or negative before price does anything else. The check is to put the round trip next to the gap. This lesson does not give you a fee from a venue. On the diagram for this beat, look for one gap wider than a two-way cost bar, and one gap thinner and crossed out. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Leave a blank labelled Round trip cost and write Look up, do not invent. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A blank you will look up is better than a fee you made up. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Fees. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

More lines are not more thorough if each gap fails the cost check. The picture gets busy and the mechanism gets worse. Busy is not the same as careful. On the diagram for this beat, look for a crowded ladder faded out beside a quieter ladder whose gaps clear a cost bar. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Circle the quieter ladder and write Clears the cost. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. You are not being given a maximum count. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Too many lines. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Recount once from a wrong page: the wrong page says twenty times a half percent equals ten percent. Correct it in writing: nineteen times a half percent equals nine and a half percent. On the diagram for this beat, look for a wrong equation crossed out and the nineteen-gap equation beside it. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Do the correction in the notebook, including both sentences. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The correction is the skill. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Worked recount. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A range needs room for the wicks you drew, not only for the closes. A band drawn on closes alone can be left by a wick that your own sketch already contains. On the diagram for this beat, look for a wick piercing a band that was drawn around closes. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Add one wick outside the closes and widen the example band to include it. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The wick is hypothetical, like the rest of the page. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Wicks. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The common miss is to change the step and the range in the same edit. Then the line count jumps for two reasons, and you cannot see which reason did it. On the diagram for this beat, look for two knobs turned at once, both crossed out, and a single-knob picture beside them. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write Change one thing. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. One change at a time is how you can still explain the page. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Common miss. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The line you keep contains a percent, the word gaps, and the word orders. If either word is missing, the line can be read the wrong way later. On the diagram for this beat, look for a single notebook line with those three items underlined. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the line and underline the three items. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A percent alone is not the line. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to What you write. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A quiet page shows the band, the gap count, and the cost check, and nothing that looks like a result. Extra ink hides the mechanic. On the diagram for this beat, look for a sparse page with three marks only. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Erase one decoration from your sketch. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Quiet is a design choice for learning, not a style prize. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Quiet page. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Recap: range first, gaps not lines, nineteen gaps in the house example, cost beside the gap, one change at a time. The nine and a half percent span is the product of the house example, not a band you are assigned. On the diagram for this beat, look for five recap chips. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Say the five chips from memory. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Entry and exit rules come next, and they use this page as an input. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Recap. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Your turn, still inside Gaps and orders. Cover the notes and say this from memory: Twenty order lines make nineteen gaps. Then uncover the diagram and check that you can still see twenty lines with nineteen marked gaps between them. Count the gaps out loud from one to nineteen on a sketch of twenty lines. Write one check question a classmate could answer from the drawing alone, and write the answer under it. The answer has to name a shape on the page. An answer about what the market will do is the wrong kind of answer. This is practice on paper. No order is sent.

Your turn, still inside The span. Cover the notes and say this from memory: Nineteen gaps times a half of one percent is a span of nine and a half percent from the lower line to the upper line. Then uncover the diagram and check that you can still see a band labelled nine and a half percent, with nineteen gaps, stamped Example. Write 19 gaps, 0.5 percent step, 9.5 percent span, and the word Example. Write one check question a classmate could answer from the drawing alone, and write the answer under it. The answer has to name a shape on the page. An answer about what the market will do is the wrong kind of answer. This is practice on paper. No order is sent.

Leave the recount on paper. Do not type it into a live ticket. The next lesson adds the stop column. The numbers stay marked Example. On the diagram for this beat, look for the notebook closed, a live form left blank. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write the next lesson's title under the recount. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Typing it live would skip the stop, which is the following lesson. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Stay on paper. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.
Next lesson: Entry and exit rules. Bring the page you just wrote. Leave every example marked Example. No order is sent between lessons.

Entry without an exit is a page that cannot finish. The exit is the stop sentence you can read when the path leaves. It is written before the entry is copied anywhere. On the diagram for this beat, look for two columns, Exit filled, Entry still empty. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Draw the two columns and fill Exit first, with Example on the page. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. This is a writing order, not a signal to enter. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hook. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

This is the Grid Bot Blueprint. The lesson is Entry and exit rules. Navy and cyan on the frame. Education only. You will write on paper before any screen.

The page has two columns: what must be true before you would start, and what finishes the idea. Both columns are sentences. A number without a sentence is not a rule. On the diagram for this beat, look for two headed columns with one sentence in each. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Title them Before and Finish. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Neither column is an order. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Two columns. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Write the finish column first. If you write the start column first, the finish column shrinks to fit a hope. The other order keeps the finish honest. On the diagram for this beat, look for a numbered 1 on the finish column and a 2 on the start column. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Put the numbers 1 and 2 on your page in that order. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Hope is not a column. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Stop first. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A finish sentence names a path: price leaves the band and does not return on the next check. You can use other words. You cannot leave the sentence blank. The lesson does not give you the price. On the diagram for this beat, look for a path leaving a band, with a blank price tag and a full sentence. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write a finish sentence with no price in it, then add Example. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Adding a live price would be a different assignment. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to A finish sentence. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

A before sentence names the sort: the path you drew is a range, the gap clears a cost you looked up, and the page has both counts. If one of those is missing, the before sentence is false and you do not copy the page. On the diagram for this beat, look for three checks feeding the before column. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Turn the three checks into one sentence. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. The sentence is a gate on paper, not a button. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to A before sentence. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

Read a worked pair of sentences aloud and point at the drawing that matches each one. If you cannot point, the sentence is about a feeling, and you rewrite it until it points. lessons.title: Lesson 1.1: What DeFi is, and the risk-first mindset

beats.vo: Lesson one point one. What DeFi is, and the risk-first mindset. By the end, you'll be able to name every layer of the DeFi stack, and ask the one question that matters before any yield: what am I being paid to risk?

Education only, not financial advice. Crypto and DeFi carry significant risk, including total loss of capital. This is general information. It does not consider your objectives, financial situation, or needs. Past or example results do not indicate future results. Consider independent advice. We do not sell or run a trading bot.
On-Chain Operator. Lesson 1.1: What DeFi is, and the risk-first mindset. The frame is navy and cyan. You will see one idea at a time, then write it down. Education only.

Here's the plan. First, what DeFi actually replaces, and the six layers underneath every app you'll ever use. Second, the three properties that make DeFi both powerful and dangerous. Third, the risk-first rule. And finally, a full worked example: a pool advertising twelve percent A.P.Y., and the five questions you ask before you believe it.
The DeFi stack.

Start with what DeFi replaces. Banks, brokers and exchanges are intermediaries: companies that sit in the middle of a financial transaction. DeFi replaces them with smart contracts: public programs on a blockchain that hold assets and follow fixed rules, for everyone, the same way, every time.

Here's the stack, bottom to top. The blockchain records every balance and transaction. Smart contracts are the protocol logic: a lending market, an exchange pool. Tokens are the assets those contracts move. Your wallet is where you hold the keys and sign actions. The interface is the website that builds transactions for you, a convenience, not the protocol itself.
And data layers, explorers and dashboards, are how you verify what actually happened.

A quick preview, because it matters for the whole stack above it. The blockchain layer isn't abstract: every action you take, in every layer above it, ultimately becomes a transaction that goes through this exact life cycle. You'll get the full picture in Lesson one point two. For now, just notice that “the blockchain records it” isn't a metaphor. It's the layer everything else sits on.

Notice where the interface sits. It's a convenience, not the protocol. A website can go down, get hacked, or be faked entirely, and the underlying contracts keep running exactly as written. That's also why a fake website is such an effective scam: it looks identical, but it's not the layer that actually holds your money.

Quick check. Is a DeFi website the same thing as the protocol it represents? The answer: no. The interface only builds transactions for you. The smart contracts are the protocol, and interfaces can be faked or compromised without touching the contracts at all.
Powerful and dangerous.

Property one: self-custody. In a bank, the bank can freeze your account, and the bank can also help you recover it if something goes wrong. In your own DeFi wallet, nobody can freeze your funds. Nobody can recover them for you either. It's the same trade-off from Module Zero, and it's worth repeating here because this whole module is built around it.

One sobering number on self-custody, from outside research, not this program. Blockchain-analytics researchers have estimated that somewhere around a fifth of all bitcoin ever mined sits in wallets that are effectively lost: forgotten passwords, discarded hard drives, seed phrases nobody can find anymore. Nobody can recover it. Nobody can freeze it either. Same coin, both directions, permanently.

Property two: composability. DeFi protocols plug into each other, like building blocks. A stablecoin can be deposited into a lending market. The interest-bearing receipt from that lending market can be deposited into a yield vault. That vault's shares can be used as collateral somewhere else. Composability is what makes DeFi powerful, letting small pieces combine into complex products.
It's also why one position can fail because of something several layers away that it quietly depends on.

Property three: transparency. Every DeFi transaction and every contract's code can be checked by anyone, for free, on a block explorer. That's genuinely powerful. But transparent doesn't mean safe. A contract can be fully visible and still contain a bug, an admin key that can change the rules, or economics that only work while a subsidy lasts. Transparency gives you the ability to check. It doesn't check for you.

Here's a real example of composability biting, not a hypothetical. In May of two thousand twenty-two, during the collapse of the Terra ecosystem, a liquid staking token called stETH briefly traded below the value of the ETH it represented, on the open market, even though it was still redeemable one-to-one over time.
Protocols that had accepted stETH as collateral, several layers away from Terra itself, felt real stress from an event that, on the surface, had nothing to do with them.

Quick check. Why can composability increase risk, even in a position that looks simple on the surface? The answer: a position inherits the failure risk of every protocol, asset, oracle and bridge it depends on, even the ones you can't see from the front end.
The risk-first rule.

Apply that rule to the stETH example from a moment ago. A risk-first operator, before ever depositing stETH as collateral anywhere, would have asked: what happens to this position if stETH trades below ETH on the open market, even briefly? That single question, asked in advance, is the entire difference between being surprised by an event and having already sized for it.

Here's the rule this whole program is built on. Before comparing returns, list what could make you lose money. A higher yield means you're being paid to carry more risk, whether or not the website mentions it. If you can't name the risk, you don't understand the yield, no matter how good the number looks.

Here's the difference between the two mindsets, side by side. Return-first starts with the number, asks how to get more of it, and treats risk as a footnote to check later, if ever. Risk-first starts with what could go wrong, sizes the position around that answer, and only then looks at whether the remaining return is worth it. Same opportunity. Completely different order of operations.

Here's what asking the question actually looks like, step by step. You see a yield. You ask what could make it fail, before anything else. You name every risk you can find: contract, oracle, bridge, peg. You size the position so that if you're wrong, it doesn't matter much. And only then do you deposit, or decide not to.
Worked example.

Question one, and the most important: where does the twelve percent actually come from? Every DeFi return is a mix of five sources. Service fees, paid by traders. Interest, paid by borrowers. Security rewards, for staking. Structural carry, like funding and basis. And incentives: emissions or points, which are only real once you've sold them. If the answer is “incentives,” that twelve percent has an expiry date.

So let's actually decompose an example twelve percent, the way an operator would. Say two percent comes from real trading fees. One percent from real borrower interest. And the remaining nine percent, the biggest slice by far, from a reward token being emitted to attract deposits. That nine percent only exists while the emissions keep flowing, and it's only real once you've sold the reward token for something else.
The headline number and the durable number are two very different things.

And four more questions, before you deposit. Which stablecoin, and what actually backs it? You'll learn to judge that properly in Lesson one point five. Which contracts hold the money, and who can upgrade them? Is there a bridge or an oracle involved, each one another thing that can fail? And how do you withdraw, and could withdrawals ever be blocked?
If you can't answer these five questions, you don't know what the twelve percent is paying you for.

One more. If nine of a pool's twelve percent A.P.Y. comes from a reward token being emitted, what should you assume about that nine percent? The answer: it's not durable. It only exists while the emissions continue, and it's only real once you've actually sold the reward token.
Last check. In one sentence, what is the risk-first mindset? The answer: identify what could make you lose money, before you compare returns.

Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, you can name the six layers of the DeFi stack. Second, you can explain why self-custody cuts both ways. And third, before any yield, you ask: what am I being paid to risk?

Let's recap. DeFi replaces intermediaries with smart contracts, across six layers: blockchain, contracts, tokens, wallet, interface and data layers. Self-custody, composability and transparency make it both powerful and dangerous. And the risk-first rule: list what could make you lose money, before you ever compare returns.

Do the checklist now, before you move on. You now have the whole lesson in your head: the six-layer stack, the three properties that make DeFi powerful and dangerous, the risk-first rule, and how to actually decompose a headline yield. Next up, Lesson one point two: How a transaction actually happens.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.2: How a transaction actually happens

beats.vo: Lesson one point two. How a transaction actually happens. By the end, you'll be able to follow a transaction from signature to finality, and estimate what it actually costs before you send it.

Education only, not financial advice. Crypto and DeFi carry significant risk, including total loss of capital. This is general information. It does not consider your objectives, financial situation, or needs. Past or example results do not indicate future results. Consider independent advice. We do not sell or run a trading bot.
On-Chain Operator. Lesson 1.2: How a transaction actually happens. The frame is navy and cyan. You will see one idea at a time, then write it down. Education only.

Here's the plan. First, the full lifecycle, every stop a transaction makes between your signature and being irreversible. Second, gas: what it is, and the two parts of its price. Third, the nonce, and why one stuck transaction can jam every one behind it. And finally, the real math: what a swap actually costs, quiet versus congested.
The full lifecycle.

Here's the complete path. You create the transaction, specifying what it does. You sign it with your private key. Your wallet broadcasts it to the network. It sits in the mempool, a public waiting room, visible to anyone. A validator includes it in a block. The network confirms that block. And after enough confirmations, it reaches finality: the point after which it can't realistically be reversed.

Here's the short version, the one worth keeping in your head day to day: sign, mempool, block, finality. Gas is paid whether the transaction succeeds or fails, because the network still did the work of checking it. That single fact explains most of what's counterintuitive about how DeFi charges you.

One more distinction worth holding onto: “pending” and “confirmed” are not the same claim. Pending means the network has seen your transaction and it's waiting in the mempool. Confirmed means it made it into a block. Until it's confirmed, anyone watching the mempool, including a rival bidder, can technically see what you're about to do and try to act first. That's part of why priority tips exist.

Notice the word “realistically” in finality. On most chains, a transaction can technically still be reorganised for a short window right after confirmation. Waiting for a few more confirmations, or for the finality rules of the specific chain and layer two you're using, which you'll cover in Module Five, is what makes “final” actually mean final.
Gas.

Gas is the unit of computation. Every operation a transaction performs, reading a balance, updating a balance, checking a signature, costs a fixed amount of gas. Your total cost is gas used, multiplied by gas price. Both numbers matter, and they move independently.

Gas price itself has two parts, on Ethereum. The base fee, set by the network based on how busy it is, and burned, destroyed, not paid to anyone. And the priority tip, an extra amount you add to get included sooner, which does go to the validator. Gas price is quoted in gwei: one gwei is one billionth of an E.T.H.

One real pattern worth knowing: priority tips spike hardest during sudden demand, a popular NFT mint, a hyped token launch, everyone racing for the same limited block space at once. That's a real, recurring phenomenon on Ethereum and similar chains, not a rare edge case.
If you're not in a race for a scarce, time-limited slot, there's usually no reason to pay the premium everyone else is paying in that moment.

Gas price isn't fixed, it's an auction for block space, and it follows real patterns. Weekday business hours in the US and Europe tend to run busier, and so does any period right after major news or a popular new app launching. Quiet periods, like weekends and the middle of the night in those time zones, tend to run cheaper.
None of this is certain on any given day, but if a fee looks unusually high, waiting an hour is often a gift.

Quick check. Your transaction fails and reverts. Did you still pay for it? The answer: yes, for the gas used up to the point of failure. The network did the computation, even though the result didn't go through.
The nonce.

Every account's transactions are numbered, in order, starting from zero. That number is the nonce. The network processes them strictly in sequence: it won't process nonce six until nonce five has confirmed, no matter how much you're willing to pay for six.

So here's what a stuck transaction actually does. You send transaction five with too low a fee, and it sits in the mempool, unconfirmed. You send transactions six and seven right after. They also sit and wait, even though they're perfectly valid, because five hasn't confirmed yet. The fix is to replace transaction five itself, same nonce, higher fee, which either confirms it or cancels it.
Once five clears, six and seven follow immediately.

When you replace a stuck transaction, you actually have two choices, both using the same nonce. Speed it up: keep the same instruction, just raise the fee, so it confirms as originally intended. Or cancel it: replace it with a zero-value transaction to yourself, at a higher fee, which uses up that nonce harmlessly and clears the jam without ever doing the original action.

Quick check. All your newer transactions are stuck pending. What's the most likely cause? The answer: an earlier nonce is stuck. Replace it or speed it up, same nonce, higher fee, and everything behind it follows immediately.
The real math.

Here's a real worked example. A swap uses one hundred fifty thousand gas. At twenty gwei, a quiet network, that's one hundred fifty thousand times twenty, three million gwei, which is zero point zero zero three E.T.H. At three thousand dollars an E.T.H., that's nine dollars. The same swap, during congestion, at eighty gwei, costs thirty-six dollars. Same swap. Same wallet.
Four times the price, because the network got busy.

And here's the number that changes everything: the same swap, on a popular layer two instead of Ethereum's main chain. Layer twos batch many transactions together and settle them back to Ethereum as one group, which typically brings the cost down to somewhere around a cent or two, not dollars. That's an illustrative, rounded range, real costs vary by network and moment, but the direction is consistent and large.
It's exactly why Module Zero has you practising on a low-fee network first.

And here's why that number matters more than it looks. If you're compounding one dollar fifty of rewards, and gas costs nine dollars, the gas costs more than the rewards. That's not a rare edge case, it's the default at small position sizes. That's exactly why position size matters on-chain, and why this program keeps coming back to it.

One more real habit: checking a transaction on an explorer. It shows the status, the fee actually paid, the sender and receiver, which contract was called, and every token transfer and log the transaction produced. Get in the habit of checking your own transactions there. It's the fastest way to confirm a transaction did exactly what you expected, and nothing more.

Last check, the numbers. Two hundred thousand gas at ten gwei, with E.T.H. at two thousand five hundred dollars. What does that cost? The answer: two hundred thousand times ten is two million gwei, which is zero point zero zero two E.T.H. At two thousand five hundred dollars an E.T.H., that's five dollars.

One more. You're about to sign a transaction, and the fee estimate looks unusually high. What should you do, in a single word? The answer: wait. Check the fee estimate before signing, every time, and if it's high, a quieter moment is often minutes away.

Put it all together, and here's the habit for every transaction you'll ever sign. Check the fee estimate first. If it looks high and you're not racing anyone, wait. Sign only once the number makes sense for what you're doing. And afterward, confirm it on an explorer: status, fee paid, and exactly what it did. Four steps, every time, and gas surprises stop being surprises.

Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, you check the fee estimate before signing. Second, you know how to find your transaction on an explorer. And third, you know a stuck transaction can be sped up or cancelled, with the same nonce and a higher fee.

Let's recap. Every transaction runs the same path: create, sign, broadcast, mempool, block, confirmed, final. Gas is computation, priced as base fee plus tip, in gwei, and it's paid whether or not the transaction succeeds. The nonce orders your transactions strictly, so one stuck transaction jams every one behind it.
And the real cost of a swap can swing four times over, quiet versus congested, which is exactly why position size matters.

Do the checklist now, before you move on. You now have the whole lesson in your head: the seven-stop lifecycle, what gas actually is, why the nonce orders everything strictly, how the real cost can swing four times over with congestion and drop by two orders of magnitude on a layer two, and how to estimate a real cost before you sign.
Next up, Lesson one point three: Wallets, keys, hardware and multisig.
